w10_T4_002752: Two collectors, Ivy and Sean, tracked seashells, and Sean's bag always held fewer than hers. Ivy started the beach trip with 64 shells in her bag, then lost 13 shells when a wave knocked her bag over. A tide pool find added 67 more shells. She then gave away 4 shells to a younger cousin, ignoring the park ranger who had tagged 500 turtles that season. Her remaining shells were split evenly across 6 jars, and only one jar was tracked. A cousin gave her 68 more shells for that jar, and a gift from her aunt made that jar's count grow to 6 times its size. How many shells were in that jar?
w10_T4_002755: A school bake sale started the morning with 23 cupcakes on the table, though a parent volunteer's 100 extra napkin sets, baked separately, were never part of the count. A fresh batch added 48 more cupcakes. A matching-donation event made the total grow to 6 times its size. A second bakery donated 34 more cupcakes. A late walk-in donor added 42 more cupcakes. Finally, a neighboring class contributed 77 more cupcakes. How many cupcakes were on the table by the end of the sale?
w10_T4_002759: A vineyard began the morning with 9 identical rows, each holding 137 grape clusters, combined into one harvest total, while a dozen crates sat empty nearby waiting to be filled later that week. By afternoon, 1056 clusters were sent to the local winery. That evening, 68 more clusters were set aside for a farmers market stand. Overnight, 40 more clusters were lost to a sudden frost. How many grape clusters remained by morning?
w10_T4_002762: Two orchard owners, Petra and Colm, tracked apple crates, and Colm's total always trailed hers. Petra had 163 crates of apples at the start of harvest. A late picking added 4 more crates. A spoilage inspection removed 130 crates that had gone bad, unrelated to the 90 empty bins stacked in Colm's shed. A regional order required her to prepare 9 times as many crates as remained. A final donation added 77 more crates. How many crates did Petra have after the donation?
w10_T4_002766: A charity relay began the morning with 218 dollars pledged, while a separate raffle table nearby sold 60 tickets that never counted toward this total. By midmorning, 73 more dollars were pledged. In the afternoon, 33 more dollars came in from a bake sale. Since the treasurer records pledges in dollars but rounds cents on the final receipt, she always double-checked totals before the bank run. By evening, 35 more dollars were pledged. Late that night, a final donor added 34 more dollars. How much money had the relay raised by night?
w10_T4_002770: A phone plan started the month with 189 minutes of data rollover. A software update used up 173 minutes right away. The remaining minutes then doubled thanks to a promotional bonus. A weekend of video calls used 16 more minutes. Since the carrier bills in minutes but the app shows usage in hours, the user always checked both numbers before month's end. A bonus top-up added 52 more minutes. Finally, 24 more minutes were used for a work call. How many minutes were left at the end of the month?
w10_T4_002779: Two bookstore clerks, Freya and Malik, tallied receipts, and Malik's total always ran behind hers. Freya's register showed 175 dollars at the start of her shift. A return refunded 87 dollars back to a customer. A bonus sale doubled her remaining total. A late rush added 16 more dollars. A closing sale added 36 more dollars. A final refund removed 9 more dollars. How much money was in Freya's register at closing?
w10_T4_002780: Two swimmers, Delphine and Otis, tracked laps, and Otis always swam fewer than she did. Delphine swam 166 laps in the first week. She skipped 39 laps during a rest week. She then missed 12 more laps due to a minor injury. A pool closure cost her 1 more lap before the meet. Ignoring the coach's unrelated count of 500 kickboards in storage, a training camp required her to complete 5 times as many laps as she had left. Her final total was split evenly across 6 training logs, and only one log was tracked. How many laps did that log show?
w10_T4_002781: A vending cart's cash box held 64 cents at the start of the morning shift. By midmorning, 34 cents were paid out in change to a customer, while a coworker's separate tip jar collected 90 dimes over at the coffee stand, unrelated to this box. A bonus deposit from head office made the remaining total grow to 5 times its size. In the afternoon, 15 cents were spent on a rubber band for the register. Since the cart logs everything in cents but the daily report converts totals into dollars, the vendor always double-checked the math before closing. By evening, a customer overpaid by 40 cents and left it in the box, and overnight, a matching fund from a sponsor made that evening total grow to 4 times its size. How many cents were in the cash box the next morning?
w10_T4_002783: A warehouse began the morning with 3 identical zones, each storing 127 boxes, combined into one inventory count. By midmorning, the stock was reorganized into 8 equally sized sections for a new layout, multiplying the total accordingly. An unrelated shipment of 300 pallets arrived at a different warehouse across town that same morning. In the afternoon, 28 more boxes were added from a late delivery. That evening, a regional distribution order required 5 times the afternoon total. Overnight, 29 more boxes were added from a returned shipment. How many boxes were in the warehouse by morning?
w10_T4_002790: A charity toy drive began with 4 identical bins, each already holding 133 toys, combined into one total. A local business added 22 more toys. A school donated 72 more toys. A weekend rush added 51 more toys. A shipping error caused 608 toys to be sent to the wrong location. A last-minute matching pledge tripled what remained. How many toys were left after the matching pledge?
w10_T4_002791: A farm stand began the morning with 102 pumpkins on display. By midmorning, 94 pumpkins were sold to early shoppers. In the afternoon, a fresh harvest added 28 more pumpkins. A festival order required the stand to prepare 9 times that afternoon total. By evening, 3 more pumpkins were added from a late pick. Overnight, 72 more pumpkins were brought in from a neighboring farm. How many pumpkins were on display the next morning?
w10_T4_002811: A toy factory started the morning with 204 robots on the assembly line. By midmorning, 40 more robots were added from a second shift. The batch was then split evenly across 4 packaging stations, and only one station's robots were tracked. In the afternoon, a bulk order required that station to prepare 6 times as many robots. By evening, 49 more robots were added from a late repair batch. Overnight, 61 more robots came off a final production run. How many robots were ready by the next morning?
w10_T4_002812: Two toy collectors, Simone and Andre, tracked action figures, and Andre's shelf always held fewer than hers. Simone started with 111 figures on her shelf, then received 5 more for her birthday. A convention purchase made her total grow to 8 times its size, while a nearby vendor's 700 unsold posters had nothing to do with her collection. She then received 67 more figures from a trade. A shipping recall removed 530 figures that were found defective. A late gift added 37 more figures, and a final bonus made her total grow to 3 times its size. How many figures did Simone have?
w10_T4_002817: A juice bar started the morning with 234 oranges in storage. By midmorning, 146 oranges were used for fresh-squeezed orders. The remaining oranges were then multiplied across 7 identical crates, each holding that same amount, for a delivery. Since the bar counts oranges by weight in pounds but sells juice by the cup, the manager kept a conversion chart posted by the register. That crate total was then split evenly among 4 delivery vans, and only one van's load was tracked. A late addition made that van's load grow to 4 times its size. A final bulk order required 5 times that new amount. How many oranges were needed for the final order?
w10_T4_002822: A car wash began the morning with 7 identical stations, each earning 79 dollars by midday, combined into one total. In the afternoon, 49 more dollars came in from a loyalty promotion. Since the shop records earnings in dollars but the franchise report converts them into a percentage of a weekly quota, the manager always did the math by hand. By evening, 496 dollars had to be paid out for equipment repairs. Overnight, a final payment added 14 more dollars. How much money did the car wash have by the next morning?
w10_T4_002825: A lemonade stand started the morning with 63 cups sold. By midmorning, 3 cups had to be remade after a spill. The stand's total was then multiplied across 8 identical pitchers, each holding that same amount, for a big afternoon batch. Since the stand tracks cups sold but the recipe card measures lemons by the dozen, the kids always converted between the two before restocking. That batch was then split evenly among 5 volunteers, and only one volunteer's share was tracked. That share was further divided evenly among 4 friends, and only one friend's share continued. A final loss of 21 cups happened when a cooler tipped over. How many cups did that friend have left?
w10_T4_002826: A print shop began the day with 8 identical printers, each producing 41 flyers, combined into one stack. By midday, 18 more flyers were added from a rush order. Since the shop counts paper in reams but bills clients per flyer, the owner kept two separate ledgers. That afternoon, 205 flyers had to be discarded after a color error. A final batch added 31 more flyers. How many flyers were left after that final batch?
w10_T4_002827: A comic book shop started the morning with 79 comics on the new-release shelf. By afternoon, 67 more comics arrived from a distributor. That evening, 81 comics were sold to eager fans. Overnight, 11 more comics were returned as damaged and removed from the shelf. A weekend restock made the remaining total grow to 3 times its size. How many comics were on the shelf after the restock?
w10_T4_002828: Two chess players, Yara and Felix, tracked their tournament points, and Felix's score always trailed hers. Yara started the tournament with 85 points. She lost 74 points after a tough defeat. A bonus round made her remaining points grow to 3 times their size. A second bonus made that new total grow to 6 times its size. A final fair-play award added 18 more points. What was Yara's final tournament score?
w10_T4_002832: Two neighbors, Priscilla and Gabe, tracked yard sale earnings, and Gabe's total, a dozen dollars behind at the start, never caught up. Priscilla's yard sale earned 70 dollars by the first hour. A late customer added 3 more dollars. A group of bargain hunters made her total grow to 4 times its size. She then had to refund 130 dollars for a broken item. A slow afternoon cost her another 62 dollars in unsold returns. A final sale added 39 more dollars. How much money did Priscilla end up with?
w10_T4_002834: A choir started rehearsal with 57 sheet music copies. The copies were then multiplied across 4 identical folders, each holding that same amount, for the sections. A second printing made that total grow to 3 times its size. The stack was then split evenly among 4 rehearsal rooms, and only one room's copies were tracked. A late addition brought 22 more copies to that room. How many sheet music copies were in that room?
w10_T4_002838: A summer camp started the week with 15 canoes available. A donation added 16 more canoes. A rental company delivered 36 more canoes for a regatta. The full fleet was then multiplied across 7 identical docks, each holding that same amount, for the big race. A final delivery added 36 more canoes. How many canoes did the camp have for the race?
w10_T4_002840: A dairy farm started the morning with 230 liters of milk collected. By midmorning, 36 more liters came in from a second herd, and the stock was then multiplied across 6 identical tanks, each holding that same amount, for the co-op pickup. In the afternoon, 46 more liters were added from a late delivery. Since the farm measures milk in liters but the co-op invoice lists gallons, the farmer always double-checked the conversion before selling. A regional order required 8 times that afternoon total. By evening, 7978 liters had to be set aside for a separate processing plant. How many liters were left for the co-op after that?
w10_T4_002846: A trading card shop began the morning with 9 identical binders, each holding 109 cards, combined into one collection. A convention order required 7 times that combined total. A second wholesale order required 7 times that new amount. Unrelated to this, a nearby comic shop sold 200 back-issue magazines that same day. A late donation added 3 more cards. A final gift added 28 more cards. How many cards were in the collection after the final gift?
